subject: paper:weyandt-2003-irs
quote: hyperactivity in adolescents and adults may be limited to subjective feelings of restlessness. Recent studies with adults with ADHD have also reported that mental restlessness is commonly reported by individuals with the disorder.
rationale: Verbatim from the PubMed/MEDLINE abstract (efetch). States the reframing directly: adult hyperactivity presents as subjective/mental restlessness rather than motor overactivity.

subject: paper:weyandt-2003-irs
quote: college students with ADHD report significantly higher ratings of internal restlessness than college students without ADHD
rationale: Verbatim from the abstract; the empirical result that the IRS separates ADHD from non-ADHD adults, giving the internalized-hyperactivity reading measured support (small-sample college study).

subject: paper:weibel-2020-adult-adhd
quote: hyperactivity is more often internalized, symptoms of inattention may be masked by anxiety symptoms or obsessive-like compensation strategies
rationale: Verbatim from the MEDLINE abstract (efetch). Independent clinician-review statement that adult hyperactivity is internalized; the same sentence flags anxiety masking, which is why this pole is hard to separate from the anxiety rival.

subject: paper:becker-2016-sct-meta
quote: SCT is a distinct symptom dimension that is separable from ADHD and other dimensions of psychopathology
rationale: Verified against the fetched full-text PDF (pdftotext). Superscript citation markers in the printed sentence ('ADHD12-35', 'psychopathology,14,25,32,37') removed; wording otherwise verbatim. Factor-analytic conclusion across >19,000 individuals.

subject: paper:becker-2016-sct-meta
quote: SCT is more strongly associated with ADHD inattention (r = 0.63 in children, r = 0.72 in adults) than with ADHD hyperactivity-impulsivity (r = 0.32 in children, r = 0.46 in adults), and it likewise appears that SCT is more strongly associated with internalizing symptoms than with externalizing symptoms.
rationale: Verified against the fetched full-text PDF; the printed '¼' ligature (an OCR/encoding artefact for '=') rendered as '='. Establishes the construct's correlate profile — closest to inattention, but pulled toward internalizing — the basis for treating it as a mood-leaning rival.

subject: paper:becker-2023-cds-consensus
quote: cognitive symptoms involving the disengagement or decoupling of attention and conscious or effortful mental processing from the ongoing external context, as reflected in difficulties with staring, daydreaming, mental confusion or fogginess, withdrawal, and sleepy appearance
rationale: Verbatim excerpt from the consensus definition (PMC full text); the cognitive dimension of CDS. Defines the foggy/daydreamy pole of the internal state that the mechanism node names.

subject: paper:becker-2023-cds-consensus
quote: SCT and ADHD-IN are empirically distinct and correlated more strongly (meta-analytic rs = .63 and .72 in children and adults, respectively) than SCT and ADHD-HI (meta-analytic rs = .32 and .46 in children and adults, respectively).
rationale: Verbatim from the PMC full text. The work-group's own statement that CDS/SCT is empirically distinct from ADHD inattention, carried by a separate source from the 2016 meta-analysis it summarises.
